title: Contingent Corporate Bill-Audit & Tax-Credit Recovery — Practitioner Testimony Operator Workbook
subtitle: A Contingency Field Workbook for Parcel Refund Recovery, Surcharge Rerating, Carrier Contract Engineering, Utility Bill Rebuilds, Indirect Expense Audits, and Property Tax Assessment Appeals

worksheets.title: Small-Parcel Refund and Surcharge Recovery Ledger
worksheets.purpose: Build a recovery ledger that captures every guaranteed service refund, blocks automatic denials, exposes auditor fee overreach, and rerates surcharges package by package so that parcel spend is both recovered and repriced on a strict contingency basis.
instructions: Grant the auditor online billing credentials for every FedEx and UPS account before completing any other field, so every invoice downloads automatically and nothing depends on manual pulls.
Freeze same-day invoice payment until every guaranteed service refund dispute is filed inside the 15-day late-package window, because an existing payment on file triggers automatic denials.
Scan the original reason column for systematic SVC fail credits before approving any auditor fee statement, and strike fees billed on refunds the carrier issued automatically.
Measure every oversize-adjacent SKU sealed, at its widest points including handles and bulges, and store the results in your own SKU dimension file before modeling any surcharge rule.
Rerate package by package with no sampling, average weights, or average zones, and send no dispute whose figures did not come from the audit itself or lack analyst sign-off.

fields.name: carrier_billing_access
fields.prompt: List every FedEx and UPS online billing account the client holds, who controls the credentials, and whether invoices can be auto-downloaded for continuous monitoring. Note any account where invoices are paid manually the moment they post, because timing matters.
fields.example: FedEx account ending 4471 and UPS account ending 2208, both held by the controller, both granted to the auditor for daily pulls. Refund Retriever describes the model as similar to mint.com, constantly using credentials to monitor invoices and shipping activity [Refund Retriever — P3sA9eO0D-k @ 00:00:52]. FedEx invoices currently auto-pay on posting, flagged for immediate change.

fields.name: payment_hold_policy
fields.prompt: Describe the current invoice payment timing and write the revised hold rule that keeps FedEx invoices unpaid until every guaranteed service refund dispute is filed inside the 15-day late-package window. Name who approves release of payment.
fields.example: Old rule: pay on posting. New rule: AP holds every FedEx invoice until the auditor confirms GSR filings are complete, then releases within the 15-day window. Refund Retriever saw a client pay as soon as the invoice was available, which caused FedEx to automatically deny any GSR service failure requests [Refund Retriever — JeLyjRF9HEk @ 00:01:25]. Controller signs each release.

fields.name: systematic_svc_fail_scan
fields.prompt: Open the FedEx online billing invoice history and record how many credits show systematic SVC fail in the original reason column. Compare that count against any refunds an auditor has billed you for, and flag every overlap for challenge.
fields.example: Last quarter showed 31 credits marked systematic SVC fail, meaning FedEx refunded those automatically. The incumbent auditor's fee statement included 12 of them. Refund Retriever warns that an auditor billing for these credits may be dishonest [Refund Retriever — 8Bw_30ivpb4 @ 00:00:48]. All 12 fee lines are disputed in writing, and the auditor must strip automatic credits from future statements.

fields.name: denied_claim_escalation
fields.prompt: Map the escalation path for every rejected service-failure dispute, including repeated resubmission, live phone follow-up, and the choice between an invalid address correction dispute, a fresh service-failure resubmission, or no further action. Assign an owner to each branch.
fields.example: Rejected disputes route first to the Share a Refund decision tree: invalid address correction dispute, resubmit the service failure, or take no further action [Share a Refund — eTB0fyueR5A @ 00:04:36]. Anything still denied goes to live phone agents. On one $4,253.53 invoice, phone calls reversed auto-denials on all 5 late packages and recovered $98.42 [Refund Retriever — JeLyjRF9HEk @ 00:01:42].

fields.name: refund_method_speed_meter
fields.prompt: Tally recovered refunds by method over the last audit period: credits on unpaid invoices, credit-card refunds, and mailed checks. Use the mix to grade whether your auditor files quickly or late, and record the percentage in each bucket.
fields.example: Invoice credits 54 percent, card refunds 30 percent, checks 16 percent. Share a Refund reads mostly invoice credits as fast filing and card credits or checks as late filing [Share a Refund — PheSsrwvW9c @ 00:04:02], and says filing claims quickly increases the success rate of the refund delivered [Share a Refund — PheSsrwvW9c @ 00:02:03]. Grade: mixed, push for faster filing.

fields.name: contingency_fee_terms
fields.prompt: Record the auditor's contingency fee percentage, the base it applies to, any volume step-downs, and whether fees attach only to refunds the auditor actually acted on. Calculate the net refund you keep on a sample recovery amount.
fields.example: Offer one starts at 50 percent of savings, so a $50 recovery carries a $25 fee, with rate negotiated down at volume [Refund Retriever — vOX4irOA_Tk @ 00:05:11]. Offer two at 30 percent leaves $700 net on $1,000 of savings [Cerasis , now part of GlobalTranz — GnXmnbxCZ-A @ 00:05:14]. Require fees only on shipments where the auditor took action.

fields.name: oversize_sku_measurement
fields.prompt: List every SKU that sits near an additional handling or oversize threshold, with sealed dimensions measured at the widest points including handles and bulges. Note the 48-inch, 30-inch, 50-pound, 96-inch, and 130-inch triggers each carton approaches.
fields.example: SKU T-220 measures 47.5 inches empty but 48.25 sealed with the bulge, crossing the additional handling line. FedEx advises measuring everything at the widest point, including handles, bulges and irregular shapes [FedEx — OpAC2Ev8SH0 @ 00:02:26]. Refund Retriever warns FedEx can remeasure in transit and hit a compliant-looking carton with a $300 oversize charge [Refund Retriever — iizNycveRfc @ 00:01:08].

fields.name: cubic_rule_exposure
fields.prompt: Using your own SKU dimension file, model exposure to the UPS 5-cubic-foot additional handling rule. Record box dimensions, actual weight, the minimum billable weight applied, the added handling charge, and the percentage change in cost per package.
fields.example: A 20x20x22 inch, 20 lb box to zone 5 rose from $19.69 to $57.18, a 190 percent increase, after the custom DIM 250 was voided, a 40 lb minimum applied, and a $36 charge added [iDrive Logistics — H64bWcLI0O8 @ 00:08:56]. Dimensions come from our own file, because most UPS billing detail carries none [iDrive Logistics — H64bWcLI0O8 @ 00:10:19].

fields.name: line_by_line_rerate
fields.prompt: Describe the scope of a package-by-package rerate: carrier, date range, invoice count, line count, and whether any sampling or average weights were used. Record the number of findings, their dollar value, and the yield as a share of audited spend.
fields.example: Benchmark: Experidium rerated 90 days of one carrier's invoices, 402 invoices and 1,870 lines, with no sampling, and surfaced 42 findings worth $11,414, or 2.38 percent of audited spend [Experidium — 8-Sguow2LDM @ 00:02:37]. Amware Fulfillment warns that discounts, minimums, DIM factors, thresholds and fuel can each swing numbers five million dollars [Amware Fulfillment — d3jQIelSHJM @ 00:19:26].

fields.name: surcharge_variance_requests
fields.prompt: List the surcharges where you will request a definition or size variance rather than a simple discount. For each, record the current trigger, the product dimension or weight that crosses it, and the revised trigger you will ask the carrier for.
fields.example: A 97-inch product against the FedEx 96-inch limit: ask to raise the limit to 98 inches, which can eliminate the fee entirely [Refund Retriever — iizNycveRfc @ 00:02:04]. A 51-pound product just over 50: push the additional handling weight trigger to 53 or 55 pounds instead of settling for a 25 to 75 percent fee reduction [Refund Retriever — TzPaNZCC4js @ 00:02:57].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not advance until FedEx payment holds are in force, systematic SVC fail credits are reconciled against every auditor fee line, a written denied-claim escalation path with named owners exists, and at least one full package-by-package rerate with analyst sign-off is complete.

worksheets.title: Carrier Agreement Engineering and Utility Bill Rebuild
worksheets.purpose: Engineer UPS and FedEx agreements around your true shipping profile, expose discounts pinned to minimum floors, protect the money-back guarantee, and rebuild every utility invoice from the rate book to recover misclassified rates and misapplied demand charges.
instructions: Assemble your own zone, weight, service and accessorial profile before the first carrier meeting, so you know your shipping better than the carrier representative across the table.
Never share your current agreement with a competing carrier, because it hands them a floor to match instead of a number to beat.
Test every proposed discount against the minimum net charge before counting savings, and plan for a negotiation cycle of 3-6 rounds over 6-10 weeks.
Pull three to five years of utility bills, tariffs, meter data and exemption certificates, then recalculate each invoice line against the rate book rather than approving any bill on its total.
Re-verify tax exemptions every billing cycle and flag every estimated read, possibly shared meter, and broken or leaking meter before trusting the usage history.

fields.name: shipping_profile
fields.prompt: Summarize your zone, weight, service, and accessorial profile in enough detail that you know it better than the carrier rep. Note your top five zones, dominant weight breaks, service mix, and the accessorials that appear most often on invoices.
fields.example: Ground is 82 percent of volume, concentrated in zones 2 through 5 at 1 to 10 lb, with residential and additional handling as the top accessorials. Refund Retriever holds that every part of the contract is negotiable and can be renegotiated at any time instead of waiting for expiration [Refund Retriever — Tu2F34LOK0g @ 00:00:30].

fields.name: minimum_net_charge_test
fields.prompt: Run each proposed discount against the minimum net charge for your most common zone and weight. Record the list rate, the headline discount, the discounted net, the minimum, and the effective discount, then estimate how much volume is pinned to the floor.
fields.example: Zone 4, 10 lb package lists at $13.27; 50 percent off yields $6.64, but the $8.23 minimum makes the effective discount 38 percent, and a 65 percent offer would save nothing [Shipware — rjelY0C_iQg @ 00:03:37]. Refund Retriever calls the minimum net charge a basement floor under discounts [Refund Retriever — JAnVvaSg0TA @ 00:03:38].

fields.name: grid_vs_tier_allocation
fields.prompt: Break each proposed discount into its guaranteed grid portion and its volume-dependent tier portion. Show the combined headline figure, the constrained figure after minimums, and the trade you will propose to shift more of the total into the grid.
fields.example: A 23 percent grid plus 12 percent tier makes a 35 percent headline, constrained to about 22 percent; LJM says maximize the grid [LJM — 56winzXYmPA @ 00:26:48]. Counter-proposal follows Scarbrough Global: concede column D from 50 to 45 percent to lift column A ground from 30 to 35-40 percent [Scarbrough Global — iflfyKDuJzY @ 00:03:59].

fields.name: gsr_waiver_strike
fields.prompt: Read every section of the proposed agreement for guaranteed service refund waiver language and list where it appears. Record the discount the carrier offered in exchange, and document your decision to strike the waiver regardless of the sweetener attached.
fields.example: Waiver language appears in the service terms and again in an addendum, so the full agreement was read twice. Refund Retriever says strike any guaranteed service refund waiver even when a hefty discount is dangled, because the language hides in multiple sections [Refund Retriever — C_7KIASDpS8 @ 00:02:41]. The offered 1-2 percent sweetener is declined and the money-back guarantee stays.

fields.name: fee_waivers_and_account_type
fields.prompt: List the administrative concessions you will request beyond rate discounts, such as waiver of the processing fee and conversion to a scan-based account. For each, note the expected billing impact and the carrier's response in each negotiation round.
fields.example: Request one: waive the 2 percent processing fee, which LJM reports gets waived about 75 percent of the time [LJM — 56winzXYmPA @ 00:18:26]. Request two: a scan-based UPS account so canceled orders and unused return labels never get billed [Good Citizens Society — 72KTU2Th6eY @ 00:02:42]. Round one response: fee waiver under review, scan-based billing accepted.

fields.name: exit_and_monitoring_plan
fields.prompt: Price the early termination fee in the proposed agreement, describe your exit path if the carrier underperforms, and set the post-implementation monitoring plan that checks every shipment for billing errors during the first months under the new contract.
fields.example: Early termination fee is quoted in six figures, consistent with what Shipware says is typical, so an exit clause tied to service failures is requested [Shipware — 6WEh56BpnbM @ 00:14:47]. Post-launch, the auditor checks every shipment, since Refund Retriever says the risk of billing errors skyrockets after a new contract is implemented [Refund Retriever — VpvZiUp02QU @ 00:02:56].

fields.name: utility_bill_inventory
fields.prompt: Inventory every utility account, meter, and service address, and record whether signed authorization exists to download historical invoices directly from each utility. Note the lookback the state allows and how many months of bills, tariffs, and meter data you hold.
fields.example: Fourteen electric, gas and water accounts across six sites, with signed authorization filed so bills come straight from each utility rather than from years of client paper [Puleo Energy — a4dO2n1QfzQ @ 00:04:47]. Target lookback is about 36 months, as far back as the state allows [Puleo Energy — a4dO2n1QfzQ @ 00:00:54]. Two water accounts the client never flagged are added.

fields.name: rate_class_check
fields.prompt: For each account, record the rate class billed, the rate class the account should carry under the tariff, and the overpayment implied by any mismatch. Note any accounts the auditor requested that the client did not know were improperly rated.
fields.example: Warehouse meter 2 is billed on the small business plan despite large-business load. Vert Energy Group cites a misclassification that caused $21,000 in overpayments over a year and a half [Vert Energy Group — bQpXnGBfNJY @ 00:02:36]. Ryan Sumerlan notes knowledge of all state tariffs lets the auditor ask for bills clients never knew were misrated [Ryan Sumerlan — h6W5k5owNiU @ 00:01:43].

fields.name: demand_ratchet_rebuild
fields.prompt: Rebuild the demand ratchet for each demand-metered account month by month. Record the highest peak across the current and previous 11 months, the calculated ratchet, the billed demand, and whether months above the ratchet were billed at actual demand.
fields.example: Peak across the 12-month window was 500 kW, so the ratchet should be 400 kW at 80 percent, yet March billed 450 kW against a 380 kW actual read. Oncor describes the ratchet as 80 percent of the highest peak across current and previous 11 months [Oncor — yHlhF0nEJ14 @ 00:01:46].

fields.name: utility_fee_agreement
fields.prompt: Record the utility auditor's contingency terms in writing: the share of refunds, the share of ongoing realized savings, the number of months savings are shared, when invoicing occurs, and the requirement that only true and uncontested findings are billed.
fields.example: Terms mirror Puleo Energy: 50 percent of refunds after the check or bill credit arrives, 50 percent of realized monthly savings for 24 months, and 100 percent to the client from month 25 [Puleo Energy — a4dO2n1QfzQ @ 00:05:57]. Billing applies only to true and uncontested findings [Puleo Energy — a4dO2n1QfzQ @ 00:06:15].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not advance until every proposed discount has been tested against the minimum net charge, all guaranteed service refund waiver language is struck, an exit path and post-implementation monitoring plan are written, and every utility account has a rate-class check and line-by-line rebuild against the rate book.

worksheets.title: Indirect Expense Audit and Property Tax Appeal Tracker
worksheets.purpose: Audit telecom, waste hauling, shipping, and workers' comp spend on a no-savings, no-fee basis, then screen owned property for assessment appeals argued on value, cap rate, and evidence, while protecting every filing deadline and avoiding counter-appeal traps.
instructions: Confirm monthly spend per indirect category and prioritize any category above $2,000 a month, keeping existing vendor relationships wherever the savings can be captured inside them.
Demand proof for every overfill or overage fee before paying it, and back-claim credits for any period in which drivers took no photos.
Confirm every disconnected telecom circuit is fully dead at the modem or NID, not merely canceled on paper, and review USF taxes and exemptions line by line.
Argue assessed value, never the bill, and build commercial appeals on the income approach and cap rate, stripping intangible value from hotel and operating business sales.
Calendar every filing deadline and 30-day change notice, walk the property for unrecorded improvements before filing, and keep prior-year taxes current past January 31.

fields.name: indirect_spend_categories
fields.prompt: List each indirect expense category under review, including telecom, waste hauling, shipping, and workers' comp, with monthly spend per category. Flag every category that clears the threshold worth a conversation and note whether recommendations can stay with existing vendors.
fields.example: Telecom $6,800, waste $3,100, shipping $33,000 and workers' comp premium tracked annually. Zog Inc sets the bar at $2,000 a month in a category as worth the conversation [Zog Inc — u-o74Ze2VNs @ 00:09:52]. Schooley Mitchell has no vendor ties, and 80 percent of recommendations involve no change of supplier [RiverForest Connections — VvAP-sQig0I @ 00:00:38].

fields.name: cfo_opening_question
fields.prompt: Write the opening question you will put to the CFO about how recovered savings will be used, and note any signs of financial stress or prospects going dark that suggest a different approach or a referral opportunity.
fields.example: Opening line: What are you going to do with the money I save you? Rob Sullivan uses that question and treats financial stress and prospects who go dark as referral cues; one client held off layoffs [Zog Inc — u-o74Ze2VNs @ 00:08:15]. Answer recorded: fund two retained positions and a delayed equipment purchase.

fields.name: telecom_circuit_audit
fields.prompt: List every telecom circuit, line, and data service still billing, and confirm which ones are fully disconnected versus half-disconnected with the modem or NID still live. Record USF taxes and exemptions line by line and any credits requested.
fields.example: Three circuits at a closed branch still bill because the NID stays live; Macronet Services hunts exactly these half-disconnected circuits and checks USF taxes and exemptions line by line [Macronet Services — QMubvpeApZk @ 00:03:13]. Benchmark: Auditel stacked $215K of additional credits on an earlier $165,000 credit across wireline, data and voice, about $370K total [Auditel, Inc. Telecom Expense Management — gIcFGhjFIKI @ 00:02:05].

fields.name: waste_contract_baseline
fields.prompt: Lock a ledger baseline for waste hauling and record the contract end date, inflation cap status, container sizes, pickup frequency, and billing basis. Note when you will approach the current hauler and competing haulers before the renewal date arrives.
fields.example: Contract ends December 31 with no inflation cap; Barracuda B2B has seen rates jump as much as 25 percent from one month to the next at year end [Barracuda B2B — vnkFP_2Jzng @ 00:03:27]. Busch Systems suggests comparing a 6-yard weekly container against a 3-yard and weighing weight versus volume billing [Busch Systems — LoP7CFupHr8 @ 00:30:02]. Hauler outreach begins in September.

fields.name: overfill_fee_challenge
fields.prompt: List every overfill, overage, or contamination fee billed by the hauler over the lookback period, whether photo proof was provided for each, and the credit you will claim back where the driver documented nothing. Include compactor charges that cannot be audited.
fields.example: A $25-a-week overfill fee appears on every invoice for three years with no driver photos. Following Paige's approach at Zog Inc, proof is demanded and three years of credits are back-claimed [Zog Inc — u-o74Ze2VNs @ 00:05:18]. The compactor is flagged too; Busch Systems calls compactors a black hole that is really hard to audit [Busch Systems — LoP7CFupHr8 @ 00:30:02].

fields.name: workers_comp_lookback
fields.prompt: Record the workers' comp policy years available for review, the classification codes assigned, credits applied, and loss reporting on file. Note the lookback the auditor will use, the error areas covered, and the contingency fee basis for any premium recovery.
fields.example: Seven policy years are on file, matching the five-to-seven-year lookbacks across 40-plus error areas that operators report. Watchdog Advisory claims 3 in 4 employers are overcharged, typically by 10 percent or more, and reports $25M recovered plus $5M in future savings [Watchdog Advisory — Joo1fuo4HkY @ 00:00:40]. Its fee is a portion of savings: no savings, no fee [Watchdog Advisory — 5eTaFaKQdHY @ 00:01:47].

fields.name: assessment_target_screen
fields.prompt: Screen each owned property for appeal potential by recording the assessed value, recent purchase price and cap rate, income approach indicators, and any intangible value embedded in a hotel or operating business sale. Rank properties by expected reduction.
fields.example: The hotel bought last year at a very low cap rate ranks first. Paramount finds about a 20 percent value change for every 1 percent cap-rate move [Paramount Property Tax Appeal — fOMz56wkRgs @ 00:00:30] and typically removes 15 to 20 percent off hotel purchase prices by stripping intangible and goodwill value [Paramount Property Tax Appeal — R_juWiwAZ-k @ 00:00:54].

fields.name: appeal_deadline_calendar
fields.prompt: Enter the original filing deadline for each property and every 30-day change notice the county sends mid-appeal. Confirm prior-year taxes are current, and name the person responsible for calendaring each date so no year is forfeited.
fields.example: Filing deadline and a 30-day change notice are entered on the tax calendar, since letting either lapse forfeits the year [Save Paulding — oIIj8lWBYVY @ 00:08:18]. Missing a deadline by a single day means waiting a full year [USA Senior Laws Guide — LopTSxbolHY @ 00:07:10]. Prior-year taxes are paid, avoiding delinquency past January 31 [Lane Property Tax Advocates — ePPknD36YQc @ 00:01:41].

fields.name: hearing_evidence_strategy
fields.prompt: Outline your hearing strategy: whether you will ask the appraiser to present first, the county evidence you have requested and when, comparable sales including off-market deals, and any request to disallow county evidence not provided in a timely manner.
fields.example: Request that the appraiser present first; in one Douglas County hearing the appraiser's own tax map showed a parcel at $12,000 an acre, cutting Roy's land from $32,000 [Save Paulding — oIIj8lWBYVY @ 00:13:11]. If county evidence arrives late, ask the chairman to disallow it [Save Paulding — oIIj8lWBYVY @ 00:22:46]. Submit the purchase contract, closing statement and appraisal for the off-market sale.

fields.name: pre_filing_risk_check
fields.prompt: Before filing, record the results of a property walk for unrecorded improvements, confirm rent roll unit counts and income are accurate, and estimate the risk of a county counter-appeal. Record the contingency fee percentage and expected net savings.
fields.example: Walk found a new roof missing from county records; filing triggers a review that can raise value [Save Paulding — oIIj8lWBYVY @ 00:04:53]. Rent roll unit counts are verified; Jimmy calls misstating them fraud [Quality Builders — tHXC3Ph5z0Q @ 00:35:04]. Fee set at 35 percent, within the 25 to 50 percent range [Cross the River, Find the Treasure — 7CfK4x3Fijc @ 00:02:40].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not advance until every indirect category above $2,000 a month has a baseline, every overfill fee and half-disconnected circuit is challenged, each appeal property is ranked with deadlines calendared, prior-year taxes are confirmed current, and a pre-filing property walk is documented.

worksheets.title: Cost Segregation Payoff and Catch-Up Depreciation Screen
worksheets.purpose: Decide whether a cost segregation study, a Form 3115 catch-up, or a Section 179D claim produces usable tax savings that clearly exceed the study fee, recapture exposure, and audit risk before any engagement is signed.
instructions: Pull the closing statement, county appraisal district land value, and placed-in-service records before entering any basis or depreciation figure.
Request the free benefit analysis first and treat its numbers as the ceiling until a full engineering-based study confirms them.
Map every projected loss to income the owner can actually offset this year, and mark suspended losses as zero savings.
Model the exit before the benefit, including hold period, recapture on sale, and any components likely to be removed.
For prior-year properties and 179D work, confirm the five-year method-change window, DCN code, third-party certification, and signed allocation letter before filing.

fields.name: property_basis_and_land
fields.prompt: Record the purchase price, closing date, and the land value you will strip out before any reclassification. State where the land figure came from, naming the county appraisal district record, and explain why no flat percentage split was used anywhere in your basis calculation.
fields.example: A $3M building closes with $2.5M of depreciable basis left after land [Engineered Tax Services — qEFJIGNNOkw @ 00:12:13]. Land is pulled from the county appraisal district record, not an 80/20, 15 percent, or 10 percent split, because Streit says those flat splits get lost in less than three minutes [Toby Mathis Esq | Tax Planning & Asset Protection — beMOZDrXOJ8 @ 00:21:41].

fields.name: reclassification_estimate
fields.prompt: Estimate the share of basis likely to move into 5-, 7-, and 15-year buckets for this asset type. Compare your property against the reclassification ranges reported for good candidates, mobile home parks, and warehouses, and note which range you are assuming.
fields.example: A suburban office building is assumed at the low end of the 25-40% band Chris Streit gives for good candidates, not the little over 80% seen on mobile home parks or the 12-15% typical of warehouses [Toby Mathis Esq | Tax Planning & Asset Protection — beMOZDrXOJ8 @ 00:15:54]. On $2.5M of basis, 25% moves $625,000 into accelerated classes for modeling.

fields.name: year_one_writeoff
fields.prompt: Model year-one depreciation with bonus against straight-line on the same basis. Show both numbers side by side, state the closing month, and confirm whether a late-year close changes the bonus result, since practitioners report bonus is not prorated.
fields.example: On the $2.5M basis, straight-line yields $64K in year one while bonus yields $794K, and $172K accelerated without bonus [Engineered Tax Services — qEFJIGNNOkw @ 00:12:13]. Because the close lands in December, the model still books about $770K versus about $6K straight-line, since bonus is not prorated [Engineered Tax Services — qEFJIGNNOkw @ 00:13:12].

fields.name: loss_usability
fields.prompt: Identify the income the year-one loss will actually offset. State whether the owner qualifies as a real estate professional or uses the short-term rental route, and describe what happens to the loss if neither applies and it becomes suspended.
fields.example: The owner has no real estate professional status and no short-term rental use, so the model mirrors Marcus, whose $55,000 loss was suspended and who saved nothing [Clint Coons Esq. | Real Estate Asset Protection — fV7tusLGp3E @ 00:04:59]. Contrast a real estate professional turning $13,120 of taxable income into a loss of about $9,308 [C2 Realty Group — dCExXUUA6zA @ 00:01:51].

fields.name: study_fee_vs_benefit
fields.prompt: Enter the quoted study fee and the projected tax impact, then compute how far the benefit clears the fee. Note whether the free benefit analysis was run first and whether the deal is too small to justify a paid study at all.
fields.example: The free benefit analysis came back in about 24 hours at no cost [Engineered Tax Services — sXpa52KOvog @ 00:25:23]. The quote sits inside the $3-6K average range [Mark Perlberg, CPA — 3bjz5YCldWA @ 00:21:12]. If projected impact lands near $13,000 to $14,000 against a $5,000 to $6,000 fee, as in Santa Monica, the study is killed [Advise RE — 8ZzVeQLb80E @ 00:02:41].

fields.name: exit_and_recapture
fields.prompt: Describe the planned hold period and the most likely exit. Estimate recapture on an early sale, list any components that may be removed before sale, and decide whether a hold shorter than five years makes the study pointless for this property.
fields.example: The owner may sell in year four, which PorterKinney says rarely justifies a study [PorterKinney — G6l9WU9XBgI @ 00:07:49]. An early sale handed back $42,500 in recapture on $150,000 of depreciation [Clint Coons Esq. | Real Estate Asset Protection — fV7tusLGp3E @ 00:09:03]. Removed assets get logged because there is no recapture on them [Engineered Tax Services — sXpa52KOvog @ 00:16:56].

fields.name: form_3115_lookback
fields.prompt: For a property placed in service in a prior year, document the Form 3115 path. Record the DCN code you will use, the sign of the 481A adjustment, and confirm no prior method change sits inside the five-year window.
fields.example: Prior returns cannot be amended for a depreciation change, so Form 3115 is mandatory [Tax Modern — hjpQzDqWetI @ 00:02:55]. The Wealthy Accountant uses DCN 8 for a permissible-to-permissible change, while Tax Modern cites 7 [The Wealthy Accountant — XhVfWjlDk3w @ 00:02:35]. The 481A adjustment is entered as a negative number [Tax Modern — hjpQzDqWetI @ 00:10:32].

fields.name: placed_in_service_and_bracket_timing
fields.prompt: Record the placed-in-service date as the day the property was ready and available for rental, not the closing date. Then state the owner's bracket this year and whether waiting for a higher bracket year before running the study makes sense.
fields.example: Closing was in March, but the unit was ready and available for rental in May, so May is the placed-in-service date [Asset Wise Institute — e9edFqL1urU @ 00:06:50]. Income is low this purchase year, so the study is deferred and run later through a 3115 once income reaches the 37% bracket [PorterKinney — G6l9WU9XBgI @ 00:08:46].

fields.name: section_179d_eligibility
fields.prompt: For design or contracting work on a commercial or tax-exempt building, test Section 179D eligibility. Record square footage, energy savings over ASHRAE 90.1-2007, prevailing wage and apprenticeship status, and the name of the independent third-party engineer certifying the model.
fields.example: A 100,000 square foot building meeting the 25% savings standard plus prevailing wage and apprenticeship moves from a $180,000 deduction under the old rule to $500,000 at $5.00 per square foot [Cherry Bekaert — JZ5NlVOVnnw @ 00:11:07]. Efficiency cannot be self-certified, so a third-party engineer is engaged before project close [Cherry Bekaert — JZ5NlVOVnnw @ 00:07:35].

fields.name: allocation_letter_leverage
fields.prompt: If the building owner is a tax-exempt or nonprofit entity, document the 179D allocation letter status. Record when you asked about allocation during bidding, the date the signed letter arrived, and anything the owner requested in exchange for granting it.
fields.example: Allocation was raised during bidding, per George Ghazarian's advice [George Ghazarian, CPA — Exr84oxoKzc @ 00:04:26]. No signed letter means no deduction, so the claim waits for it [George Ghazarian, CPA — Exr84oxoKzc @ 00:04:54]. The campus owner asked for an extended warranty period in exchange, a trade nonprofit clients have negotiated before [Cherry Bekaert — zU4xMPqHWY0 @ 00:06:46].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not engage a study or file a Form 3115 until land value comes from the county appraisal district, the year-one loss maps to usable income, projected tax impact clearly exceeds the fee, the hold period exceeds five years, and any 179D claim has third-party certification plus a signed allocation letter in hand.

worksheets.title: Work Opportunity Tax Credit Screening and Claim Mechanics
worksheets.purpose: Build a hiring-to-filing pipeline that screens every new hire, lands Form 8850 and ETA 9061 inside the 28-day window, proves hours and wages, and documents every adjacent credit or refund claim so it survives verification.
instructions: Start from actual hiring volume and turnover, then decide whether to self-file or outsource screening and state reporting.
Design screener questions around the target groups that actually generate certifications, using exact Form 8850 language.
Treat 28 calendar days from each start date as a hard wall and send both forms together as they come in.
Hold the credit off the books until the final determination letter arrives, then prove hours and wages before Form 5884.
Keep a retention file for every claim, and confirm substantiation exists before pushing any R&D, sales tax, or 179D benefit.

fields.name: hiring_volume_and_credit_value
fields.prompt: Record annual new-hire volume and turnover, then estimate potential credit value using the $2,400 typical figure and the higher veteran amounts. Note whether volume crosses the roughly 50-hires-per-year line that practitioners use to justify outsourcing the screening and state filing.
fields.example: The restaurant group hires about 120 people a year, well above the roughly 50 hires where ADP outsourcing at about 25 percent of the credit becomes worth it [Linked Accounting, LLP — yEWXbR-V5qs @ 00:01:01]. For scale, a Five Guys franchise projected $27,600 from 86 qualifying hires after first adopting screening [Official ReadyATS — KqRldQ_XlyA @ 00:06:18].

fields.name: target_group_mix
fields.prompt: List the target groups your applicant pool most likely falls into and the expected share of each. Do not assume veterans and ex-felons dominate; compare your expectations against the reported split between SNAP recipients and veterans among actual certifications.
fields.example: The screening plan assumes SNAP households will drive most certifications, since Lydia at Workstream reports about 70 percent of qualified hires are SNAP recipients and only about 7 percent are veterans [Workstream — 3hIbQPQR66Y @ 00:20:13]. Veteran hires are still flagged because the top credit reaches $9,600 for disabled-veteran groups [Workforce3One — w5ydUbSH5TI @ 00:00:23].

fields.name: screener_question_design
fields.prompt: Draft how screener questions will be presented to applicants. Specify whether ex-felon and veteran questions are separated from SNAP, welfare, and residency questions, whether wording follows Form 8850 exactly, and how age-related eligibility is asked without asking age directly.
fields.example: Ex-felon and veteran questions move to a separate screen, because Lydia reports applicants are about 20 percent less likely to finish when they see ex-felon wording [Workstream — 3hIbQPQR66Y @ 00:06:34]. All remaining questions use exact Form 8850 language, and the form asks about SSI benefits rather than whether someone is over 65 [Workstream — 3hIbQPQR66Y @ 00:14:58].

fields.name: screening_timing
fields.prompt: Decide when Form 8850 reaches the candidate: before the offer, at the job offer, or alongside the I-9 during onboarding. Record the reasoning behind that choice and how the chosen point integrates with your applicant tracking or electronic onboarding system.
fields.example: The 8850 is handed over at the job offer, which IRS liaisons call best practice [VA OSDBU (On Demand) — onLA9L1sYIc @ 00:49:10]. In electronic onboarding it sits right next to the I-9, since much of the I-9 data is what the 8850 asks for anyway [The TLC Companies — kuYWnLG5-A4 @ 00:19:52]. Pre-offer screening, which Workstream pushes and MP discourages, is declined.

fields.name: twenty_eight_day_tracker
fields.prompt: For each new hire, log the start date, the calculated 28th calendar day, and the submission method. Confirm both Form 8850 and ETA 9061 travel together, and confirm forms go out as they arrive rather than being batched for later.
fields.example: A cook starting March 3 gets a March 31 wall date. Both forms go together, because you cannot send just one [Jason D. Knott — RmnPUe0eO7s @ 00:08:06]. Packets are uploaded as they arrive, never batched [MP: Wired for HR — tAf8rI1hwtc @ 00:25:25]. Past 28 days, Gift CPAs says don't bother, the state gives no credit [Gift CPAs — RzWkA9XcT7g @ 00:05:34].

fields.name: submission_method_compliance
fields.prompt: State exactly how packets reach the state workforce agency. Confirm whether you use the e-file portal or mailed packets with a real postmark, and list any methods you have ruled out because the agency does not accept them for timeliness.
fields.example: All packets go through the state e-file portal. Mailed backups carry a real post office postmark, because SC DEW says postage meter stamps do not satisfy the postmark rule and email or fax submissions are not accepted [SC DEW — ujWX1IZPyFc @ 00:07:11]. Late filings sit on the ineligible list alongside rehires, relatives and 1099 workers [SC DEW — ujWX1IZPyFc @ 00:05:22].

fields.name: special_population_timing
fields.prompt: Identify any hires from special populations, such as justice-involved transitional workers, whose eligibility depends on when the application is filed. Record the status at filing and confirm the timing preserves eligibility rather than converting the person into an ineligible rehire.
fields.example: A transitional worker from a corrections work program receives an offer for permanent employment. The application is filed while the person is still a transitional worker, because after release they count as a rehire and no longer qualify [Louisiana Dept of Public Safety and Corrections — xtpFtLZJyrM @ 00:14:04]. The hire date and filing date are both recorded in the tracker.

fields.name: hours_and_wage_proof
fields.prompt: For each certified hire, attach W-2 wages and a payroll register showing hours worked. Mark whether the hire cleared 120 hours for the 25 percent tier or 400 hours for the 40 percent tier on the $6,000 wage base.
fields.example: One certified hire worked 450 hours, clearing the 400-hour tier, so 40 percent of $6,000 yields $2,400. Another worked only 20 hours in the year, which yields zero credit [Jason D. Knott — RmnPUe0eO7s @ 00:11:55]. W-2 wages and the payroll register for both are pulled before Form 5884 is prepared [Buffalo Tax Strategies — AUiM2KAknsw @ 00:03:38].

fields.name: vendor_fee_and_booking
fields.prompt: If a screening vendor is used, record the contingency percentage, when the invoice is issued, and when payment is due. Then state your booking rule: confirm the credit is not booked until the final state determination letter arrives.
fields.example: The vendor charges 20 percent, invoices only after a credit exists, and expects payment only after the credit is used against tax [The TLC Companies — kuYWnLG5-A4 @ 00:17:36]. Credits stay off the books until the final determination letter arrives, with state waits budgeted at up to a year or longer [Gift CPAs — RzWkA9XcT7g @ 00:05:51].

fields.name: adjacent_claim_documentation
fields.prompt: List the retention file for every WOTC claim, then note any adjacent claims in flight, such as R&D credits, sales tax refunds, or 179D. For each, state what substantiation exists today and which election or certification deadline could close.
fields.example: WOTC files keep 8850s, SWA transmittal letters, proof of mailing and certifications, generally for three years [Gift CPAs — RzWkA9XcT7g @ 00:09:14]. A pending sales tax refund needs an audit trail for the entire audit period [Sales Tax Sisters — LibBgjGxja4 @ 00:05:34]. The R&D team notes the 280C election keeps 79 percent of the credit [Cherry Bekaert — nR3lgfqRNqg @ 00:13:08].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not claim any WOTC credit until every hire has a logged 28-day wall date, both forms reached the state by portal or true postmark, the final determination letter is on file, payroll proves the 120 or 400 hour tier, and the retention file is complete for each adjacent claim.

worksheets.title: Contingency Fee Vetting and Reverse-Audit Recovery Plan
worksheets.purpose: Vet every contingency or shared-savings arrangement against a defensible baseline, then run your own look-back across sales tax, workers' comp, customs, CAM, and contractor rates to find overpayments the other side's audit will never surface.
instructions: Get the fee percentage, billing trigger, and full scope in writing before any contingency firm touches your records.
Lock the baseline from your own ledger and validate any third-party or payer data before accepting it.
Model every threshold, corridor, or tier before counting shared-savings cash, and reject metrics the paid party cannot control.
Set look-back windows by statute, extend them where an open audit allows, and demand source documents before paying any true-up.
Install a prevention control the day the refund lands so the same overpayment never recurs and a follow-on audit runs smoothly.

fields.name: contingency_engagement_terms
fields.prompt: Record the proposed engagement's fee percentage, what triggers billing, and the scope of work the firm performs. Confirm whether the firm handles everything from identification to check in hand, and whether any cost is owed when nothing is recovered.
fields.example: The sales tax reverse-audit firm confirms in writing that it does 100 percent of the work from identification to check in hand on a 100 percent contingent basis [PM Business Advisors — ePf76grjr8U @ 00:01:32]. Aaron Hall's warning that contingency lawyers look out for themselves first is the reason the scope and fee trigger are written out line by line.

fields.name: baseline_definition
fields.prompt: Define the baseline against which savings or recoveries will be measured. Name the data source, the period it covers, who validated it, and whether any third-party or payer-supplied figures were checked independently before being accepted as the starting point.
fields.example: The baseline is twelve months of invoiced spend pulled from the general ledger, then cross-checked with operational staff before the contingency firm starts. Payer and vendor data are never taken at face value, echoing Forster's rule: do not just trust the data because the payer said so [Garrett Schmitt — UEDbkKJ-9Xk @ 00:18:12]. Benchmarks can be gamed [Health Affairs — Zzb5OKFwcbg @ 00:22:28].

fields.name: gainsharing_metric_design
fields.prompt: If the arrangement shares savings with physicians or operating partners, describe each metric, who controls it, and the payout structure. Record the share paid out, and show whether payouts use tiers or a single all-or-nothing threshold that could zero out.
fields.example: The physician share is capped at 50 percent, the ceiling Fredrikson's speakers would defend, versus a 75 percent deal they would not do [Fredrikson — VMuMGmjYplc @ 00:28:18]. On-time starts pay at 85/90/95 percent tiers, because a single 90 percent trigger zeroed a $100,000 bonus at about 87 percent after anesthesia and nursing delays [Fredrikson — VMuMGmjYplc @ 00:20:34].

fields.name: minimum_savings_threshold
fields.prompt: Identify any minimum savings rate, corridor, or floor that must be cleared before shared savings pay out. Model expected savings against that threshold and state what portion, if any, flows back to your organization at the projected savings level.
fields.example: Projected savings of 2.5 percent sit under the roughly 3 percent corridor, where the ACO gets 20 percent and CMS keeps 80 percent [Reyann Davis — EotsrYaUjUs @ 00:07:45]. No cash is counted yet, because about 160 participants in 2018 generated savings and received no check due to the minimum savings rate [COPE Health Solutions — PDcTn9Sq3mg @ 00:21:31].

fields.name: contingency_plan_and_release_controls
fields.prompt: Document any operational contingency plan or contract contingency tied to this recovery effort. Record where the plan lives, the date it was last reviewed and tested, and the conditions that must clear before any contingency release is signed.
fields.example: The supplier contingency plan moves out of email into the controlled document system and is reviewed within twelve months, since a 15-month-old, email-only plan drew a major nonconformance [IATF 16949 Auditing — 4-TMYIb48FA @ 00:04:38]. On the facility purchase, no full release is signed until inspection, appraisal and loan conditions clear [Jeb Smith — HDpLh9uRXMo @ 00:21:54].

fields.name: reverse_audit_lookback
fields.prompt: Set the look-back window for your sales and use tax reverse audit. State the statute of limitations in each relevant state, note any open audit that extends the window, and list purchase categories most likely to contain overpaid tax.
fields.example: Most states in scope allow three years, one allows four, and an old audit still open in the third state lets the review reach seven to ten years back [PM Business Advisors — ePf76grjr8U @ 00:00:30]. The look-back exists because state audits are pro state and agents do not weigh pro-taxpayer provisions [Carr, Riggs & Ingram — HpOuVeLrWBs @ 00:00:42].

fields.name: workers_comp_and_customs_review
fields.prompt: List the workers' compensation and customs items you will reexamine for overpayment. Note classification codes, credits, and loss reporting for workers' comp, and for imports confirm that entry values, invoices, payments, weights, quantities, and dates line up before filing any refund.
fields.example: Workers' comp review covers classification codes, credits and loss reporting over three years, the scope behind a $190,000 Kentucky manufacturer recovery [Greg Walker — sM254iPKhSo @ 00:02:41]. Before any CAPE upload, the team adds 80 days to each liquidation date, confirms a US ACH account in ACE, and confirms no drawback on any entry line [Flexport — xtorVFI9g4c @ 00:47:05].

fields.name: cam_reconciliation_review
fields.prompt: Before paying any CAM reconciliation invoice, list the documents you will demand from the landlord and the lease terms you will test. Note caps, exclusions, gross-up, and controllable-expense definitions, and describe how you would handle an unusually large true-up.
fields.example: The tenant requests the general ledger, big-ticket invoices and controllable-expense definitions, then checks caps, exclusions and gross-up [Commercial Real Estate Escalations Made Simple — CWHu33HRBVY @ 00:01:42]. An extra $30,000 water main break in the true-up is negotiated into repayment over several months rather than one bill [Coastline Equity — u1Y-WxOKXpc @ 00:09:18].

fields.name: rate_renegotiation_ask
fields.prompt: For any contractor rate renegotiation, such as a FedEx CSA, record the exact dollar figure you will request and how it was built. Note the submission lead time, the tracking method for your unique characteristics file, and any early-acceptance bonus at stake.
fields.example: The ask is an exact figure, like the $121,417.12 Route Consultant cites as proof of homework [Route Consultant — 39UxCZgtvHU @ 00:23:22]. Unique characteristics go out four to six months early through a Google link that shows opens [Route Consultant — 39UxCZgtvHU @ 00:24:34]. Negotiating forfeits nothing, since the 1 percent early-accept bonus rolls into rates [Route Consultant — -AnzYDP3LQw @ 00:04:13].

fields.name: post_recovery_controls
fields.prompt: Describe the controls you will install once the refund or savings lands so the same overpayment does not recur. Name who owns each control, how purchases or invoices get checked going forward, and how you would prepare for a follow-on audit.
fields.example: Purchasing now asks the tax team whether a machine or new-vendor item is taxable before buying it [Cherry Bekaert — S7Qlojol4pE @ 00:09:00]. The refund file stays audit-ready, since that same client was hit with an audit after the refund and it went smoothly [Cherry Bekaert — S7Qlojol4pE @ 00:05:53]. The controller owns the check and reviews exceptions monthly.

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not sign any contingency engagement or pay any true-up until fee terms and scope are written, the baseline is validated against your own ledger, every threshold and tier is modeled, look-back windows are set by statute, source documents are in hand, and a named owner holds each post-recovery control.
